evals.name: review-diff-with-duplication
evals.prompt: Review my current diff before I merge. I added a formatDate helper in src/orders/utils.ts and a CSV export in src/reports/export.ts; I think it's fine but double-check it.
evals.expected_output: Recalls first (cortex search for the area's conventions); reads the full touched files, not just the diff; runs dup_scan on the touched tree and context_map on the area; flags the new date helper if an equivalent already exists, naming both locations and proposing the shared unit; sweeps the AI failure modes (dead or debug code, missing error handling, convention drift, hallucinated APIs); output follows the review format: Summary, Blocking / Should-fix tables with File:line and a concrete fix, Nice-to-have, What's good, Verdict; any convention relied on or established is recorded in cortex without secrets

evals.name: refactor-without-behavior-change
evals.prompt: Refactor src/services/payment.ts. It's 600 lines, has three near-identical retry loops, and some functions nobody seems to call anymore. Keep the behavior the same.
evals.expected_output: Searches cortex for existing payment/retry conventions before editing; builds a context_map of the area and reads the whole file; uses dup_scan to confirm the clones and extracts one shared retry unit instead of adding a new helper when one already exists; removes only symbols confirmed to have 0 references, not just ones that look unused; keeps public signatures that are load-bearing (high reference count) or flags any change to them; keeps error handling and timeouts, no leftover console.log or commented-out code; runs the existing tests to prove behavior is unchanged; persists the decision/pattern to cortex

evals.name: parameter-scalability-question
evals.prompt: Is this signature going to hold up as we grow? function fetchUsers(orgId, includeInactive = false, limit = 50, useCache = true, legacyMode = false)
evals.expected_output: Applies the parameter & scalability lens: for each parameter says what it does, why it exists and who passes it (checking call sites and reference count with context_map when code is available); flags boolean flags that switch behavior (legacyMode, includeInactive, useCache) as possible split functions or an options object; flags the hardcoded limit and missing pagination as a 10x-scale risk; notes that changing a high-reference signature is load-bearing and needs a migration path; gives a concrete proposed signature; answers in the user's language and does not invent call sites it did not read
